notes.engine: Only the rules DECLARED in tests/engine-manifest.js — Tier A (zero dependencies, forever) and Tier B (bound). engine-boundary.test.js fails the day a Tier A rule grows a require. The other 117 files in lib/ are adoption and infrastructure, counted there not here.
notes.middleware: Every file in middleware/ — what decides who may do what, before a route sees the request. The database-side half of the same job is RLS, which is on the database row.
notes.web: The 24 capabilities app.html loads on demand (cap-*.js), and the 26 SHARED files they lean on — core.js, cart.js, the language packs, the test board’s own verdict and menu shape. ⭐ Shared files were absent from this row until 2026-09-12, so the web layer was reported at the size of its capabilities alone. ⚠ CO-ASSIST is here under its OLD NAME: cap-workforce.js. The React pages in src/ and the standalone screens (till.html, promo.html, shop.html, iot-howitworks.html) are neither, and are still not counted.
notes.api: One entry per route file, sized in COSMIC function points (ISO/IEC 19761) rather than lines. ⭐ ACTOR IS THE MODEL UNDERNEATH ALL OF THIS: actors.js is the "B3 Actor model API", and a person, a co-assist and a connector are each an actor — which is why the word turns up wherever you look. integrations.js is the declared HOME of connectors (catalogue, kit download, heartbeat); connectors.js is the actor + its connections. ⚠ assist.js is NOT the co-assist — it is the tier-1 LLM proxy, so a model key never reaches the browser.
notes.database: Every TABLE the 196 migrations create — not the migrations themselves, which are changes rather than things. There is no schema document to read: the migrations ARE the schema, so they are read for what they add up to. ⭐ RLS IS THE COLUMN THAT MATTERS, and it says one of three things. · POLICY: the database itself keeps one entity's rows away from another's. · SHARED: the table has no entity column at all — blueprints, capabilities, AI skills, the standards register. Every entity reads the same rows, there is nothing to isolate, and a policy here would be wrong. This is a correct state, not a missing one. · ⚠ UNGUARDED: it HOLDS entity rows and has no policy. That is the only one of the three that is a finding, and there are 17 of them. ⚠ They were all printed as "none" until 2026-09-12, which made the 43 correct ones look like failures and hid the 17 real ones among them. ⚠ Born-in is where each table came from; later ALTERs are followed for added columns only, so this is an inventory, not a live schema dump.
notes.bridge: THE CROSSING, and the half of the product's name that had no row until 2026-09-12. ⚠ NOT A NEW LAYER — every file here also sits on another row, which is the point: a crossing is something the layers DO, not a place. This row answers the question the architecture rows cannot: which code decides that this chit reaches THIS entity and no other, and what rights travel with it. ⭐ IDENTIFY resolves a typed name to one identity or refuses (404, never best-effort delivery). ⭐ CROSS mints ONE COPY PER PARTICIPANT — never shared, always replicated — and freezes the clearances, the governance and the retention floor onto each copy at that moment. ⭐ PROTECT is RLS: after it lands, the database itself refuses rows that are not yours. ⚠ THE KNOWN GAP: the crossing is NOT TAMPER-EVIDENT. chit_hash exists on cb_chit, the RETIRED table; the live chit_header has 22 columns and no content hash. Identity is proven, ownership is enforced and rights are frozen — but nobody can later prove a copy is byte-identical to what was sent, which is exactly what a dispute needs. See BACKLOG-test-cases.md.
notes.connector: ONE CONCEPT, and routes/connectors.js declares it: "L3.1+ : a connector = a first-class ACTOR (identities row) grouped by SITE (Model 1), holding its connection string (IoT: CB-issued ActorKey+endpoint, or your broker · ERP: base_url+auth_ref), owning CONNECTIONS (devices/endpoints) each with its own bridge_id + config. Health is last_seen-based and CASCADES: a Pi/system offline => every connection under it reports no-signal (the sensors may be fine, the pipe is down). Every route is auth'd + gated on the entity's 'connector' capability. (b62 schema.)" ⭐ So IoT and ERP are not two subjects — they are the two shapes of ONE connection string, and routes/integrations.js adds that a downloaded kit IS a co-assist connector. That is why co-assist, IoT, ERP and Tally all land here, and why ACTOR is the word you meet first. ⚠ The list below is the FILES: ADAPTER (one per foreign system), KIT (the spine that drives them), CHANNEL (how a chit reaches a person). IoT has no adapter among them — its 3 file(s) are the signal blueprint and the lifecycle scripts, and it becomes a row the day it is written as an adapter.

middleware.name: idempotency
middleware.purpose: server-side idempotency for the offline OUTBOX (Phase 2). A mutation carrying an `Idempotency-Key` header is executed AT MOST ONCE per (entity, key): the first request runs and its response is recorded; any REPLAY with the same key returns the recorded response WITHOUT re-executing — so an outbox replay on reconnect can never mint a second chit / form / credential. Concurrent in-flight duplicate → 409; same key reused with a DIFFERENT body → 422. Opt-in (no header ⇒ untouched) and SELF-HEALING (store missing ⇒ proceeds without idempotency, never breaks a request) so it is safe to deploy before b109 is run. Scoped per entity, WITH RLS (via withEntity).

connector.name: csv
connector.purpose: ADAPTER: any system that can export a CSV and read one back — the proof that the core is system-neutral.

connector.name: gofrugal
connector.purpose: ADAPTER: GoFrugal RetailEasy / HQ — its "WebReporter" API on the retailer's own server (grocery and pharmacy POS).

connector.name: tally
connector.purpose: ADAPTER: Tally Prime / Tally.ERP 9 — over its own XML port (Gateway of Tally › F1 Help › Settings › Connectivity: "Enable ODBC/XML" on port 9000). Two functions, as every adapter: readProducts() and pushOrder(order) — plus the optional readStock() · readProfile() · pushReceipt(p) (a Receipt voucher when the seller marks the chit paid, 2026-09-05).

connector.name: zoho
connector.purpose: ADAPTER: Zoho Books (REST) — the shape a hosted system attaches through: fetch() instead of a local port.

connector.name: core
connector.purpose: ChitBridge connector CORE — the half that talks to ChitBridge. Adapters (./adapters/*.js) talk to the outside system.

connector.name: setup
connector.purpose: THE ONLY SCREEN THE CONNECTOR HAS: a short conversation in the console (Athi, 2026-09-05: "how will they upload the key, where is it supposed to be — within Tally? does our connector open any screen?").

connector.name: beckn-map
connector.purpose: The Beckn <-> chit mapping as a readable TABLE plus a small applier. 22 assertions. Deliberately UNWIRED: alignment you can review and reject, with no new surface area to confuse the Saturday team run.

connector.name: channels
connector.purpose: the CHANNEL MAP: which inbound number / address belongs to which entity.

connector.name: whatsapp-media
connector.purpose: fetch the BYTES of a photo a customer sent, so a co-assist can read it.

connector.name: whatsapp-out
connector.purpose: NOTIFY BACK. A chit's status change reaches the customer on the channel they wrote in on.

connector.name: whatsapp-templates
connector.purpose: the ONLY thing that may be sent outside Meta's 24-hour window.

bridge.name: chits
bridge.purpose: Resolution in order of how STABLE an identifier is, never how convenient: entity_id, then bridge_id, then user_id (the handle), and display_name only as a LAST resort — a display name is a VIEW name, free to change. ⚠ Two guards stop a chit reaching the wrong party: status must be active, and a minted party (user_id ~) can NEVER be resolved by name, because minted suppliers carry ordinary shop names and a name typed by any business could otherwise reach another business's private supplier record. Nothing resolves → 404 and the send is refused.

bridge.name: handle
bridge.purpose: What a handle IS: athi.clothing — a name a person can say out loud, exactly two levels, chosen at registration and never changed. Pure, no database.

bridge.name: mint
bridge.purpose: The SHAPE of a chit in one place, so four minting paths agree on what one is.

bridge.name: readiness
bridge.purpose: What gets FROZEN onto the copy at the crossing: the sender's held clearances and assurance rung, snapshot per copy. Later changes never alter a copy that has already crossed.

bridge.name: workpattern
bridge.purpose: The governance stamped onto the crossing: constitution, capability, work pattern and standards, resolved at send and carried as lineage.

bridge.name: policy
bridge.purpose: Retention is PER COPY and each owner sets its own floor — MAX, never MIN. A counterparty may ask you to keep a record longer and you will; they can never make your copy disappear sooner.

bridge.name: auth
bridge.purpose: Who is asking, before any route sees the request.

bridge.name: index
bridge.purpose: Sets app.current_entity on the transaction — the value every RLS policy reads. This is the seam the whole isolation model hangs on.

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Repeated tap raises the quantity
cases.pre: Counter paired; at least one product on the shelf.
cases.data: Any product with a price.
steps: Open the Sell screen.
The shelf list is shown on the left, the cart on the right.
Tap a product once.
One line appears in the cart, quantity 1.
Tap the SAME product again.
Still ONE line. The quantity box now reads 2.
Tap it a third time.
Quantity box reads 3, and the line total is 3 × the unit price.
cases.note: The first fault reported. The quantity was always right underneath; the box never repainted, so it read 1 beside ₹150 of a ₹50 item.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Enter adds the product that was typed
cases.pre: Sell screen open.
cases.data: The full name of a product that is NOT first in the list.
steps: Type the product name in full in the search box.
The list narrows; the typed product is highlighted.
Press Enter.
THAT product is added — not the first row of the list.
cases.note: Reported as "Enter adds the wrong product".
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Search finds a name ending in a letter or a number-word
cases.pre: Sell screen open; a product named like "Nandhini milk 500 ml" exists.
cases.data: na m 500
steps: Type: na m 500
Nandhini milk 500 ml appears in the results.
Search a product whose name ends in a single letter (e.g. "Probe biscuit A").
It is found.
cases.note: "a", "an" and "oru" mean ONE to the numeral reader, so "Probe biscuit A" became "Probe biscuit 1" and matched nothing.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: An offer on the shelf comes off the bill
cases.pre: A live offer exists that covers a category (e.g. buy 2 get 1 on Biscuits).
cases.data: Three units of a product in that category.
steps: Find a product showing an offer badge on its shelf row.
The badge names the offer.
Add three of it to the cart.
The cart line shows the discount.
Read the totals.
"Saved" shows the discount and TOTAL is reduced by it.
cases.note: The cart described a line without its category, so a category offer could never match — while the shelf badge did. The shelf promised what the bill refused.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: The shelf row states the price fully
cases.pre: Sell screen open.
cases.data: Any product.
steps: Read one shelf row.
It shows: what one costs · per what unit · whether tax is included · the MRP struck through with the saving, when there is one.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: A tiered price changes at the break
cases.pre: A product with a tiered pricing structure exists (e.g. 10+ at a lower rate).
cases.data: Buy 1, then buy the tier quantity.
steps: Add ONE of the tiered product.
The line uses the list price.
Raise the quantity to the tier break (e.g. 10).
The unit price CHANGES, and the line says "10+ price".
cases.note: The biggest fault found overnight: the counter skipped pricing entirely, so a tiered product billed at list price at the till while the storefront re-priced it. Same goods, two prices, depending which door the customer came through.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Quantity can be changed from the cart
cases.pre: At least one line in the cart.
steps: Press − on a cart line.
The quantity falls by one.
Press + on the same line.
It rises by one.
Press Ctrl + Up arrow.
The LAST line rises by one AND the product list does not scroll or move.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: The count and the tax split are shown
cases.pre: A GST-registered shop; three products in the cart totalling five items.
cases.data: 3 products / 5 items.
steps: Read the cart heading.
It reads "3 products · 5 items".
Read the totals block.
Taxable, then CGST and SGST on separate lines, then GST total.
Add CGST + SGST by hand and compare with GST total.
They are exactly equal (e.g. 3.34 + 3.33 = 6.67).
cases.note: CGST takes the rounded half and SGST the remainder — the tax engine's own rule.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: Money is grouped the Indian way
cases.pre: A bill or figure over ₹99,999.
steps: Look at any figure over ₹99,999.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Selling
cases.intro: The four faults reported first, and the two found while fixing them.
cases.title: A product with no price says so
cases.pre: A product exists with no price set.
cases.data: That product.
steps: Add it to the cart.
It goes on the bill.
Read the line.
The counter says "has no price — it will add nothing".
cases.note: A priceless product is a FREE product. The health check reported it, but only to someone who opened the health check.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Getting paid
cases.intro: How a bill is settled, and what gets recorded about it.
cases.title: The payment method is stated before it is recorded
cases.pre: At least one line in the cart.
steps: Read the line under the Cash / UPI / Card buttons.
"This bill will be recorded as Cash."
Tap Card.
The sentence changes to say Card.
cases.note: It always recorded Cash by default. If the customer paid by UPI and nobody tapped it, the drawer count is short by exactly that, and nothing said so.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Getting paid
cases.intro: How a bill is settled, and what gets recorded about it.
cases.title: UPI shows a QR for the amount due
cases.pre: Shop has a UPI payee declared in Settings; a bill open with an amount due.
steps: Tap UPI.
A QR code appears.
Read beside the QR.
It shows the amount, the payee id, and "The shop marks it paid here once the money arrives."
Scan it with any UPI app (do NOT pay).
The app shows the shop name and the correct amount.
cases.note: Nothing confirms the payment. The money moves bank to bank — a counter claiming to have SEEN it would be lying about what it cannot observe.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Getting paid
cases.intro: How a bill is settled, and what gets recorded about it.
cases.title: The payee name a customer will see is checkable
cases.pre: Shop has a UPI payee declared.
steps: Open ☰ → Health check.
The panel opens.
Find the line about the payee name.
It reads "Paying you shows the name <your shop name>".
cases.note: That name appears in the customer's app before they press send. If it were a machine handle, that is how they decide not to.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.module_name: Getting paid
cases.intro: How a bill is settled, and what gets recorded about it.
cases.title: A bill can be split across two methods
cases.pre: A bill with a total over ₹500.
cases.data: Take ₹500 in cash, the rest by UPI.

cases.title: Append-only — a history can be added to and never shortened
cases.pre: The test lab open (🧪 Test lab), with at least one case loaded.
cases.data: Any case.
steps: Mark a case Pass.
It shows as passed.
Mark the SAME case Fail, with a note.
It shows as failed — the latest word wins.
Press History on that case.
⭐ BOTH results are listed, oldest at the bottom. The Pass was not replaced.
Mark it Pass again and re-read the history.
Three entries. Nothing was ever overwritten.
cases.note: ⭐⭐ This is what append-only MEANS to a person: "it failed on Thursday and passed on Friday" is a sentence that survives. ⚠️ The mechanism — cb_app may INSERT and SELECT and nothing else — is a database grant no screen can show you, and is proved by tests/test-board.test.js. This case proves the consequence: that a flaky thing is visible as pass·fail·pass rather than collapsing into whatever was tapped last.

cases.title: Idempotency — the same bill twice is still one bill
cases.pre: The counter, paired, with the internet ON.
cases.data: Any product.
steps: Turn the wifi OFF and complete a bill. Note its number.
The bill saves and waits to be sent.
Turn the wifi ON and press Send now (F8 → Send now).
It sends.
Press Send now again, twice.
Nothing is sent a second time — the queue is empty.
Open the app and find that bill number in Order.
⭐ ONE chit, not two or three.
Read the total on the chit against the slip.
The same. The customer was not charged twice.
cases.note: ⚠️⚠️ A replay is ROUTINE, not an error — the counter bills offline and replays its queue whenever the line returns, so the same bill number arrives more than once as a matter of course. The bill number rides as `client_ref` and the server answers a repeat with the chit that already exists. ⭐ Two vouchers in the books for one sale is the thing this prevents.

cases.title: Jurisdiction — the country decides the rules, not the code
cases.pre: ⚠️ NEEDS A SHOP THAT IS NOT IN INDIA. Set the country in Settings, or register a second shop.
cases.data: Compare against a shop in India.
steps: Open the counter for the non-India shop and make a bill.
It bills normally.
Read the bill number.
⭐ It carries NO Indian financial year — no "26-27" anywhere in it.
Open ☰ → the checks list.
A note says the numbering rules for that country have not been checked.
Read the note.
It says the numbers are unique and sequential, and that the length, characters and annual reset have NOT been confirmed for that country — only for India.
Compare with an Indian shop's bill.
That one DOES carry 26-27 and resets in April.
cases.note: ⭐⭐ The 16-character cap, the April–March year and the annual reset are all India GST rules, and all three were about to be written into the counter where nothing would announce them. A Dubai shop whose numbers restarted every April could not have told — it would just see numbers. ⚠️ The note in the checks list is the honesty: we say what we have NOT checked rather than showing a green tick.

cases.title: gettext — a missing translation reads as English, never as a key
cases.pre: Signed in. A language pack other than English available (Arabic, Tamil, Hindi or French).
steps: Switch the language from the avatar menu.
The labels change.
Read every menu item and button on the screen.
⭐ Anything not translated shows in plain ENGLISH.
Look for anything that reads like a code — "nav.catsetup", "btn.save", "till.print".
There is none. Not one label on any screen.
Open two or three more screens and look again.
Still none.
cases.note: ⭐ gettext's rule, adopted rather than invented: the English string IS the key, so `tx('Save & print')` returns the English when no pack carries it. ⚠️ A key-based layer degrades to "till.save_print" on screen, which is worse than the English it replaced — and it is always the reader who least expected it who sees it.

cases.data: A priced product.
steps: Open the counter for that shop.
Shelf prices show that shop's symbol — not ₹.
Build a bill and read the totals.
Same currency throughout.
Open the shop screen (promo.html) on a second display.
Same currency. NOT rupees.
Print or preview the slip.
Same currency on every figure.
If the currency has no decimals (JPY), check a price.
No decimal point at all.
If it has three (KWD, BHD, OMR), check a price.
Three decimal places.
cases.note: ⚠️⚠️ THE SCREENS HAVE ONLY EVER BEEN PROVEN IN RUPEES. The renderer is proven per currency by a guard; no spec drives a non-INR shop end to end, and the money-language legend card says so in its own gap list. ⭐ This case is that gap. The shop screen once hard-coded ₹ and en-IN — so a Dubai shop showed dirham prices with a rupee sign, on the one screen a customer reads with nobody beside them to correct it.

cases.title: ECMA-402 — the CURRENCY groups the amount, not the reader
cases.pre: Any shop. Best seen on an Indian shop that also quotes a foreign currency.
cases.data: A price over ten lakh — 1234567.50.
steps: Look at a large RUPEE figure on any screen.
₹12,34,567.50 — lakh grouping, which is how rupees are written.
Now look at the same size figure in DOLLARS.
Check a euro or a dirham figure.
Also three-three-three.
Check the DECIMALS on each.
Those follow the currency too — two for most, none for JPY, three for KWD.
Switch the interface language, then look again.
⚠ The figures are UNCHANGED. Labels and dates follow the reader; the amount does not.
cases.note: ⚠⚠ THIS CASE ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE UNTIL 2026-09-11 AND WAS WRONG. Athi: *"an Indian shop quoting $ cannot use the Indian standard — everyone understands currency standard globally, but not the Indian standard"*, and *"Indian standard is for Indian rupees only"*. ⭐ The distinction the old rule collapsed is that AN AMOUNT OF MONEY IS CONTENT, NOT PRESENTATION: a chit travels to a counterparty whose locale we cannot know, and the figure is the thing being sent. ₹12,34,567.50 is how rupees are written to anybody anywhere; $12,34,567.50 is how dollars are written to nobody at all. ⚠ PKR, BDT, LKR and NPR are conventionally lakh-grouped too and are NOT in the table, because that is not verified — a guessed convention on somebody's invoice is worse than the plain one.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

steps: Open the test lab board → Summary.
Sittings are listed.
Find the automated run.
It shows its kind (unit / t1) and its totals.
Open it.

cases.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 — the report does not sign itself
cases.pre: The test lab board, with some results recorded.
steps: Open the Report tab.
A Test Completion Report, naming the standard it follows.
Read the sections.
Ten of them, numbered.
Find the green "Measured" sections.
Overview, results by feature, incidents, blockers, reusable assets — built from the ledger.
Find the amber "Needs a person" sections.
⭐ Deviations, completion evaluation, residual risks, lessons, approval — each carrying a QUESTION, not an answer.
Read section 6, the completion evaluation.
It states how many cases have never been run, and how many cite a clause that has since changed.
Read section 10.
Signature lines. No name, no date, nothing claiming an approval.
cases.note: ⚠️⚠️ HALF A COMPLETION REPORT IS JUDGEMENT and no database holds any of it. A generator that fills those headings with plausible prose produces a document that LOOKS signed off and is not — read by people who were not in the room and cannot tell invented text from evidence. ⭐ 29119-3 is the CURRENT standard; IEEE 829 is the name most people reach for and was withdrawn in 2013.

cases.title: The product list is walked with the arrows, and the marked row is the one that acts
cases.pre: Counter on Sell, with more than a screenful of products.
steps: Press Tab.
The mark moves to the product list. A message says so.
Press ↓ three times.
The mark moves down three PRODUCTS — not three category chips.
Press ↑ once.
It moves back up one.
Press Enter.
The MARKED product is added — not the first in the list.
cases.note: ⚠️ The category chips sit before the list in the page, so Tab found them first and the arrows then walked categories while the operator believed they were walking products. Fixed 2026-09-10; this case is what keeps it fixed.

cases.title: Page keys move a screenful; Home and End reach the ends
cases.pre: Counter on Sell, list focused (press Tab first), more than two screenfuls of products.
steps: Press PageDown.
The mark jumps roughly a screenful down, and the list scrolls to follow it.
Press PageUp.
Back up by the same amount.
Press End.
The mark goes to the LAST product in the list.
Press Home.
Back to the first.
At the very top, press PageUp again.
It stays at the first row — it does not wrap to the bottom or go blank.
cases.note: ⚠️ The edges are the half that breaks: a page key that runs past the end of the list either wraps (so the operator loses their place) or lands on nothing (so the next Enter adds nothing, silently). Both read as "it did not work" and neither is reported precisely.

The quantity of THAT line rises — not the last line added.

cases.title: F2 gets you back to the search box from anywhere
cases.pre: Counter on Sell.

The box is empty.
Click somewhere else entirely — the bill, a total.
Focus is away from the search box.

The cursor is in the search box, ready to type or scan.
Type or scan immediately.

cases.title: F4 re-reads the shop without losing the bill in progress
cases.pre: Counter on Sell, with two or three lines on an UNFINISHED bill.
steps: Note what is on the bill.
Two or three lines.
Press F4.
The counter re-reads the shop — prices and products refresh.
Look at the bill.
⭐ STILL THERE. Every line, every quantity, unchanged.
cases.note: ⚠️⚠️ A refresh that clears a half-built bill is the single most expensive small bug a counter can have: the customer is standing there and the operator has to start again from memory. cases.title: F6 parks a bill and you can get it back
cases.pre: Counter on Sell, a bill with lines on it. ⚠️ SELL MODE ONLY.
steps: Build a bill with two lines.
On screen.
Press F6.
The bill is parked. The screen clears for the next customer.
Serve another customer and finish their bill.
Normal.
Bring the parked bill back.
Both lines are there, with their quantities.
Now press F6 in RECEIVE mode.
Nothing happens — parking is a sell-mode idea.

cases.title: F9 finishes whatever you are doing, in every mode
cases.pre: Counter open. ⚠️ Do this in ALL THREE modes.
steps: In SELL mode with a bill on screen, press F9.
The bill is finished — payment, then the slip.
In RECEIVE mode with a goods receipt open, press F9.
The receipt is confirmed.
In DESPATCH mode with a despatch open, press F9.
The despatch is confirmed.
In SELL mode with an EMPTY bill, press F9.
Nothing is created — it does not make a bill for nothing.
cases.note: ⭐⭐ F9 is the commit key, and the same finger does all three jobs. ⚠️ The last step is the one that matters: a commit key that fires on an empty document puts a zero-value voucher in the books, and nobody notices until the series has a hole in it.

cases.pre: Counter on Sell, with some bills done today. ⚠️ SELL MODE ONLY.

Day close begins — it asks about the cash drawer.
Read what it says.
It states what it counted and what it expected.
Cancel.
Nothing is closed. The day continues.

cases.title: In the app: ? shows the keys, / searches, c composes
cases.pre: Signed in to the app (not the counter).
steps: Press ?
An overlay lists the keyboard shortcuts.
Press Escape, then press /
The cursor lands in the search box on whatever screen you are on.
Press Escape, then press c
Compose opens.
Click into any text box and type "c".

cases.module_name: Engines — the answers that reach the screen
cases.intro: Three engines with no case. ⚠️ One of them (numerals) has no guard either, which is the more serious half: these cases check that the right answer reached the screen, not that the arithmetic is right.
cases.title: Numerals — a spoken or typed quantity becomes the right number
cases.pre: The counter, on Sell. Quantity entry by typing (e.g. "3*" before a product) or by speech if enabled.
cases.data: A product priced per kilo.
steps: Enter a quantity of 3 the ordinary way.
Three on the line.
Enter "10" as a quantity.
Ten — not one, not five.
If speech is enabled, say "two kilo".
Two. Not one.
If Tamil is enabled, try "pathu" (ten).
⭐ Ten. This is the exact word that once came back as 5.
Try "oru" (one) followed by another numeral — e.g. "oru pathu".
⚠️ It does NOT read as 1. "oru" is one ONLY when no other numeral follows it.
cases.note: ⚠️⚠️ NUMERALS ARE A CLOSED CLASS — about forty tokens per language, finite, and then done forever. That is why it is a table and not a prompt: asking a model to be reliable about the closed half is paying per call, forever, for something a table settles once. ⭐ AND lib/numerals.js CURRENTLY HAS NO UNIT TEST — a table one typo away from halving an order, with nothing checking it. That guard matters more than this case does.
cases.run_by: a person on the board (a customer, and it is UAT)

cases.title: Lot fields — what a consignment must carry, asked once and kept
cases.pre: Counter in RECEIVE mode, recording a goods receipt for a product that tracks lots or batches.
cases.data: A product with a batch or expiry requirement.
steps: Start a goods receipt for that product.
The lot fields are asked for — batch, expiry, whatever it declares.
Leave a required one blank and try to confirm.
It refuses and says which field.
Fill them in and confirm.
The receipt is recorded.
Find that receipt again.
⭐ The lot details are still on it — they were not asked for and then dropped.
Now do the same for a product that does NOT track lots.
No lot fields are asked for at all.
cases.note: ⭐ The arithmetic and the field rules are already covered by tests/lotfields.test.js — this is the human half: that the fields appear for the products that need them, refuse to be skipped, and survive onto the record. ⚠️ A field asked for and then discarded is worse than one never asked, because somebody typed it believing it mattered.

cases.title: The payment QR encodes this shop, this amount, this bill
cases.pre: ⚠️ NEEDS A SHOP WITH A PAYEE ADDRESS CONFIGURED (e.g. a UPI id). Tally Test Shop has none — payWays() correctly offers only Cash and Card there, which is not a bug.
cases.data: A bill with a known total.
steps: Build a bill with a memorable total.
On screen.
Choose the QR payment method.
A QR code is shown.
Scan it with a phone.
The payment app opens with the shop as payee.
Read the NAME the app shows.
It is the shop's name — the one the checks list warned you it would show.
Read the AMOUNT the app shows.
⭐ Exactly the bill total. Not the subtotal, not the pre-offer figure.

Unchanged and unpaid — showing a code is not recording a payment.

What is ours is WHAT WE ENCODE: the payee, the amount and the reference. ⭐ An amount that is a rupee out, or a stale payee, is money going to the wrong place or the wrong sum arriving — and the customer finds out, not the shop.

cases.module_name: Waiting — what a second of somebody else's day costs
cases.intro: Two screens measured by a stopwatch and a person's patience. ⚠️ The trip counts behind them are guarded automatically; these ask the question the counts are a proxy FOR.
cases.title: Changing a chit's status answers without a pause
cases.pre: Signed in as an entity with at least one chit in a state that can advance (pending → accepted, accepted → completed). ⭐ Do this against the LIVE server, not localhost — the distance is the point: the app runs in San Francisco and the database is in Mumbai.
cases.data: One ordinary chit. A second hand or a phone stopwatch.
steps: Open the chit and press the button that advances its status.
The result appears. Time it.
⭐ Judge it as a shopkeeper would, not as a developer.
Under about two seconds it feels like a button. Past four it feels broken, and people press it twice.
Advance a chit to completed specifically.
⚠️ This is the expensive one — completing also FREEZES the invoice on your copy. It should still answer in the same breath.
Press the same button again on the same chit.
It says it is already in that state and answers immediately — it does not error, and it does not do the work twice.
Do twenty in a row, as if closing a day's tasks.
⭐⭐ THE REAL TEST. One slow button is an annoyance; twenty is the complaint that started this work.
cases.note: ⚠️ MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: one status change was 29 round trips across the Pacific; it is 22 now, 18 of them before the answer is sent. The rest is a courtesy notice to a customer who wrote in on WhatsApp, which runs AFTER the response on purpose and must never make anyone wait. ⭐ If this case fails while tests/round-trips-chit.test.cjs is green, the trips are not the problem and somebody should say so on the board rather than re-cutting a path that is already cut.

cases.data: A stopwatch.

It is on screen quickly enough that you do not look away.
Open a second one, then go back to the first.
⭐ The second open should not be slower than the first — nothing is warming up per chit.
Open one with attachments.
The chit appears; the attachments may fill in after. ⚠️ Waiting for a file list before showing the chit would be the bug.

Still usable. This is where a spare round trip is actually felt.

It offers to register, and says what registering gets you. It does not dump you on a login form with no explanation.
Start registration and read every field before typing.
⭐ Each field says what it is for. Nothing asks for something a shopkeeper would not have to hand.
Enter the business details and continue.
It moves on. Anything it refuses, it refuses with a reason you could act on.
Complete the verification step.
The code arrives, and entering it finishes registration.
Land in the app for the first time.
⚠️ You can tell what to do next. An empty app with no first instruction is a failure of this case even if registration worked.

cases.module_name: Registering a business
cases.intro: The first five minutes, done by somebody who has never seen this before. ⚠️ Run it on a genuinely new business — a second registration on an existing one takes different paths and proves less.
cases.title: The user id rule is enforced, and explained before it is broken
cases.pre: On the registration screen, at the field that asks for the business user id.
cases.data: Try: a 4-character id · a 30-character id · one with a space · one with a dot or slash.
steps: Read the field before typing anything.
⭐ It says the rule UP FRONT — the length allowed, and that spaces and special characters cannot be used because they are reserved.
Enter something too short (4 characters).
Refused, and the message says the minimum. It does not just go red.
Enter something too long (30 characters).
Refused, with the maximum stated.
Enter one containing a space.
⚠️ Refused — and the reason given is that the character is reserved, not merely "invalid".
Enter a valid one and continue.
Accepted.
cases.note: ⚠️ THE ID IS COMBINED WITH OTHERS LATER — an employee becomes `business@person`, a local supplier `~business.sup-01`. cases.title: The country is asked, and it changes what follows

cases.data: Register once as India; if you can, look at what a non-India choice offers.
steps: Reach the country question.
It is asked plainly, and early.
Choose India and continue.

cases.title: The business signs in and lands where it left off
cases.pre: A registered business. Signed out.
cases.data: The business user id and its password.
steps: Sign in with the correct details.
You are in, and the screen says which business you are signed in as.
Close the tab and open the app again.

Sign out deliberately.
You are out, and back on a screen that offers to sign in.
Press Back in the browser.

cases.title: Wrong details are refused without saying which half was wrong
cases.pre: On the sign-in screen.
cases.data: A real user id with a wrong password; a user id that does not exist.
steps: Sign in with a real id and a wrong password.
Refused.
Sign in with an id that does not exist.
Refused.
⭐ Compare the two messages.
⚠️⚠️ They say the SAME thing. A message that distinguishes them tells a stranger which business ids are real, which is how a list of targets is built.
Try several wrong passwords in a row.
It slows down or stops you. Unlimited free attempts is the finding.

cases.module_name: Signing in
cases.intro: The step between having an account and doing anything. ⚠️ Worth its own module because two different kinds of person sign in here — the business itself, and an employee acting for it — and they must not land in the same place with the same powers.
cases.title: An employee signs in as themselves, not as the business
cases.pre: A business with at least one co-assist created (Menu → Co-assists).
cases.data: The employee id in the form `business@person`, and their own password.
steps: Sign in as the employee.
You are in, and the screen names the PERSON, not just the business.
Look at what is on the menu.
⚠️ Less than the owner sees, and what is missing is missing — not present and then refused when pressed.
Do something that records who did it — a status change, a note.
The record carries the employee’s name.
⭐ Sign in as the business in another browser at the same time.
Both work. One does not evict the other.
cases.note: ⭐ A co-assist acts FOR the business: the data belongs to the business, the action belongs to the person. ⚠️ If a screen shows the business name where the person did the work, the audit trail is wrong in the one way nobody notices until it matters.

cases.title: [OFF-03] A CUSTOMER-ONLY OFFER THROUGH THE SUPPLIERS MENU. Athi, 2026-09-06: "assume Chola Auto Care is the registered customer of tallytest — can he pass additional off through the link? … so each customer gets a personalised discount"; "see how you can pass customer based discount through supplier menu". The seller writes "Regulars 10%" Only for → New customers. A buyer who has never traded sees the list price (₹200) and no badge; the anonymous storefront payload carries no such offer at all.
